issues.description: Deprecation message omits the target version where removal occurs in user-facing warning text consistency.
issues.detail: The decorator message states removal in Falcon 5.0, and the docstring directive says deprecated since 4.3. Both are correct, but the test only matches the trailing sentence. A stricter test would assert the version string too, so future message edits surface in CI rather than silently passing.

issues.description: Literate comment opportunity: explain why contextlib is preferred, not just that it is.
issues.detail: The docstring deprecation note tells the reader what to use but not why the stdlib version is sufficient (thread-safety, reentrancy, identical semantics for the documented use). A one-line rationale would let a careful reader migrate without rerunning the code to verify equivalence. Small literate-programming polish, not load-bearing.

issues.description: Test asserts behavior but does not verify stderr path is still wired correctly under deprecation.
issues.detail: The new test exercises only the stdout branch. The function takes both stdout and stderr; a complete audit would assert that the deprecated wrapper still redirects stderr as documented, since the deprecation decorator wraps the generator and a careless refactor could break one branch silently. Two extra lines, full coverage of the invariant.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED but essentially correct. This is a small, well-scoped deprecation: decorator added, internal call sites migrated, news fragment written, deprecation test included. The algorithmic content is trivial (a context manager swapping sys.stdout/sys.stderr), so complexity and data-structure questions do not apply. My only notes are literate-programming polish: the docstring could state why contextlib suffices, the test could cover the stderr branch as well as stdout, and the warning-match assertion could pin the version string. None of these block merge.
